query: As-cast HfMoTaTiZr has high strength at room temperature and elevated temperature but a relatively high density of 10.21 g cm−3. What single intervention could reduce its density without sacrificing its mechanical properties at room temperature and at elevated temperatures, including approximately 1000 °C? State the proposed intervention and mechanism, predict directional changes relative to as-cast HfMoTaTiZr, define the applicable temperature and loading boundaries, identify supporting prior evidence, and propose an experiment and rejection criterion that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Adding a lightweight element, such as Al, to the HfMoTaTiZr high-entropy alloy can reduce its density without sacrificing its mechanical properties at room temperature and elevated temperatures.
generation.intervention: Adding a lightweight element, such as Al
generation.conditions: Room temperature and elevated temperatures (up to 1000 °C)
generation.mechanism: Derived from materials-science principles, as the records do not provide a direct mechanism for the target system. The addition of a lightweight element can reduce the density of the alloy while maintaining its strength due to the solid solution strengthening effect.
generation.predicted_outcome: Reduced density without sacrificing mechanical properties
generation.boundary: Temperature range: room temperature to 1000 °C, loading conditions: compression and tension
generation.uncertainty: The exact amount of density reduction and the effect on mechanical properties may vary depending on the specific composition and processing conditions

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare samples of HfMoTaTiZr high-entropy alloy with varying amounts of added Al, and test their mechanical properties at room temperature and elevated temperatures
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the addition of Al does not reduce the density of the alloy or sacrifices its mechanical properties, the hypothesis is falsified

Abstract: AbstractNowadays refractory high-entropy alloys (RHEAs) are regarded as great candidates for the replacement of superalloys at high temperature. To design a RHEA, one must understand the pros and cons of every refractory element. However, the elemental effect on mechanical properties remains unclear. In this study, the subtraction method was applied on equiatomic HfMoNbTaTiZr alloys to discover the role of each element, and, thus, HfMoNbTaTiZr, HfNbTaTiZr, HfMoTaTiZr, HfMoNbTiZr, HfMoNbTaZr, and HfMoNbTaTi were fabricated and analyzed. The microstructure and mechanical properties of each alloy at the as-cast state were examined. The solid solution phase formation rule and the solution strengthening effect are also discussed.
